A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Word Tokenizer research. Their main texts, tables, figures, mathematical notation, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across substantial relocation of content.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP classification, subgroup robustness, BLIP captioning, and inference-efficiency experiments, including supplementary ablations in Appendices B and C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for random token dropping and combining VWTs with 8-bit quantization.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains variance-based patch dropping, pixel-space clustering and cosine-threshold matching, and averaging embeddings after adding positional information. CLS handling and batch padding are unchanged. Random dropping and joint quantization are evaluated as controls or compatibility configurations; the proposed VWT algorithm is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Waterbirds, CelebA, MetaShift, OpenImages common/rare, COCO, NoCaps, and ImageNet-1K vocabulary construction. Classification, subgroup robustness, ordinary and long-form captioning, and online versus batched inference are retained. The added experiments use existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds random token dropping as a comparison control for variance-based dropping in Appendix 7.1 and Table 9. Base, Q8, ToME, and the existing random-merging control remain. Newly cited distillation and fine-tuning methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate random dropping at ratios 0.25, 0.33, 0.5, and 0.7, and apply Q8 jointly with four VWT configurations. The reported benchmark splits, metrics, image sizes, backbones, and principal batch-size-one setting remain unchanged. Newly specified efficiency-measurement details are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices 7.1–7.2 add substantive tests of the variance-based selection criterion and compatibility with quantization across classification, robustness, and captioning. Table 4 also extends the embedding-space ablation with OpenImages results. Existing random-merging, threshold, dropping-ratio, fairness, vocabulary-sparsity, and batching analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 systematically removes the ± uncertainty values reported throughout v1's main and supplementary tables. It also removes the explanation that variance was estimated by shuffling samples across splits while preserving subgroup proportions. No replacement uncertainty analysis is provided, and the PDFs do not establish whether run counts changed.

E6.justification: v2 adds result sets for random dropping and joint quantization, efficiency measurements for 100- and 10,000-word vocabularies, and OpenImages embedding-space token lengths. Newly reported COCO power for the 100-word tokenizer is 144.71 W. Shared point estimates remain unchanged, including vocabulary-size performance results moved from v1 Table 10 into v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: The encoder and token-count formalization is retained. Distinguishing the embedding dimension with d-hat is a notational clarification; no substantive mathematical reasoning, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract's maximum wattage-reduction claim increases from 19% to 25%, supported respectively by the 1,000-word tokenizer on CelebA and newly reported 100-word tokenizer measurements on COCO. This changes the claimed efficiency envelope across configurations. The central training-free tokenization and online-inference contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix 7.1 adds hypotheses about random dropping affecting gender features versus background correlations and explicitly discusses variance-based dropping mistakenly removing foreground objects. Appendix 7.2 adds arguments about compatibility with other compression techniques. Existing interpretations of threshold sensitivity, subgroup disparities, embedding-space matching, and batching limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the NVML power query, averaging measurements across samples, an isolated measurement environment, image-encoder-only timing/power, and exclusion of vocabulary preprocessing. Code and checkpoint links remain unchanged. Conversely, v1's explicit disclosure that BLIP omits the caption prefix 'a picture of' is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references concerning distillation, memory-efficient fine-tuning, and token selection, including AMD, MEFT, and Simoulin et al. It also explains that Token Pooling is excluded as a baseline because its code was unavailable. The central positioning relative to ToME, visual codebooks, and NLP tokenization is retained.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is extensively reorganized into Sections 4.1–4.9. Former Appendix B.1–B.3 analyses enter the main text, batching moves to Appendix 7.5, and Appendices A–C are redistributed into Sections 6–7. Dataset descriptions and explanatory prose are rewritten, with terminology standardized around pixel space and subgroup robustness.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 are expanded and restructured, v1 Figures 4 and 7 are combined into v2 Figure 5, and numerous tables and figures move between the main text and appendices. Two new experimental tables are added. Existing patch visualizations and batch-size plots retain their underlying graphics despite relocation.

improvement.justification: The new random-dropping and quantization controls strengthen experimental scrutiny, while the measurement disclosures clarify what the efficiency results represent. However, v2 removes uncertainty estimates and their estimation description throughout the paper, weakening assessment of robustness and efficiency differences. Most earlier results are otherwise retained. These material gains and losses do not support a reliably assessable net direction in overall quality.
